messages.author: 75e0b0abcbafbc7d
messages.subject: Re: {Suspected Spam} [distance-sampling] Manual Formula for ESW
parts:
Ahmad

Effective strip width (ESW) is the distance at which the number of detection at greater distances is equal to the number of animals not detected at smaller distances.  ESW is not the average of your detected distances.

You can calculate ESW by hand as the product of the truncation distance (w) and the estimated detection probability (p).

The output you provide shows the estimated detection probability to be 0.68 and ESW of 13.4. From this I conclude that your truncation distance (w) was 19.7, is that correct?

It is not simple to calculate detection probability (p) by hand; that is why we developed the Distance for Windows software. As I noted, the estimate of (p) is shown in the output you provided.

To calculate (p) by hand, you would need to integrate the detection function with the estimated detection function shape (and perhaps scale) parameters.
